questions.q: How does lift depend on speed?
options: In proportion to speed and air density
It does not depend on speed

questions.q: The stall speed in a turn at 60° of bank, compared with level flight, is:
A normal static margin in pitch is:
options: CG behind the neutral point by 5%
CG exactly at the neutral point, for minimum drag
CG ahead of the neutral point by 5–15% MAC
CG ahead of the neutral point by 50% MAC
questions.explain: The CG is ahead of the neutral point by 5–15% of the mean chord.

questions.q: Dive test: after you release the sticks the plane keeps diving. This is:
options: Too far forward a CG, the elevator is overloaded
An aft CG, a small margin
questions.explain: A stable plane pulls out to level by itself.

options: Airspeed only, with the elevator holding altitude
The total energy of the aircraft
questions.explain: The elevator distributes energy between altitude and speed.

questions.q: AIRSPEED_MIN relative to V_s should be:
questions.explain: A margin for turns and gusts.

questions.q: Where, roughly, is the neutral point of a flying wing?
questions.explain: With corrections for sweep; the CG goes at 15–20%.

questions.q: Cruise speed relative to stall speed is roughly:
questions.explain: Cruise is chosen with a margin of ≈ 1.4 times the stall speed.
